title: arXiv Physics Daily — Friday, 30 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-recent ordering, not a popularity ranking. At the 2026-10-31T01:27:43Z snapshot, Semantic Scholar had zero citation and influential-citation totals for all seven newly announced papers, leaving little citation evidence; independent mentions, acceptance status, cross-lists and concrete results therefore carry more weight.

sections.title: Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS) VIII. First interstellar detection of fully deuterated methyl cyanide
sections.abstract: Using ALMA observations of L1551 IRS5, the authors report the first interstellar detection of fully deuterated methyl cyanide (CD3CN) and a deuteration pattern that informs competing molecule-formation pathways.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify CD3CN, along with two less-deuterated isotopologs, toward L1551 IRS5N2; they say the increasing D/H ratios are consistent with cold dust-grain chemistry but leave room for warm gas-phase production or earlier formation.
sections.evidence_type: observational; ALMA COMPASS 12-m array spectral survey with LTE radiative-transfer modelling
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis concerns one protostellar source and assumes LTE; the authors note that no astrochemical model yet treats methyl-cyanide deuteration through CD3CN, so the inferred formation route is not settled.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An independent Astrobiology.com item covered the result on 30 October; arXiv records acceptance for Astronomy & Astrophysics. The first-detection claim is specific and directly testable against the ALMA spectra.

sections.title: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate single- and two-qubit gates in a cryogenic cesium tweezer array, reporting 99.970(2)% single-qubit fidelity and 99.76(8)% raw entangling-gate fidelity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a cryogenic 133Cs array with a 99.970(2)% single-qubit Clifford fidelity and 99.76(8)% raw two-qubit CZ fidelity, using direct single-photon coupling to a Rydberg P state.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; randomized benchmarking and coherent control measurements in a 4 K cryogenic optical-tweezer atom array
sections.unique_caveat: The measured two-qubit infidelity is dominated by atomic motion, according to the authors; the reported results do not yet demonstrate scaling to a large array or fault-tolerant operation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A public quantum-experiment tracker opened a same-day item linking the paper and its two-qubit fidelity; the work also reports a complete universal gate set in cryogenic hardware, a clear platform milestone.

sections.title: PRISMS GHZ8: Evidence for a Young Burst and Potential Merger Activity at z=10.23
sections.abstract: JWST spectroscopy and imaging of the z=10.23 galaxy GHZ8 reveal two close components and support a very young star-forming episode, while a merger-driven burst remains a possibility rather than a demonstrated cause.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a short, recent burst or less than 50 Myr of continuous star formation in GHZ8-main; the compact companion's very blue continuum implies a young, low-ISM component with estimated ionizing-photon escape fraction 0.6–1.0.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST/MIRI LRS spectroscopy combined with NIRCam imaging, NIRSpec/prism data and SED fitting
sections.unique_caveat: The merger-induced-starburst interpretation is explicitly tentative and needs deeper imaging or spatially resolved kinematics; the inferred properties also depend on spectro-photometric calibration and SED modelling.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines new JWST/MIRI line spectroscopy with NIRCam morphology and reports approximately 5σ Hβ–[O III] and 4σ Hα detections. Its physical interpretation is salient to early-galaxy evolution, but independent coverage was not found in the sources checked.

sections.title: Entanglement diagnostics of stochastic-resetting steady states: theory and measurement on superconducting qubits
sections.abstract: The authors derive entanglement diagnostics for quantum spin chains with stochastic resets and test them on an IBM superconducting processor, finding close agreement for entropy measures but suppressed concurrence.
sections.claimed_result: For the systems studied, the entropy Jensen gap equals the subsystem's Holevo information about time since reset; IBM processor entropy measurements track noiseless predictions without fitted parameters, while concurrence is lower than prediction.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and theoretical; exact transverse-field Ising-chain calculations up to 12 qubits and measurements on an IBM superconducting processor
sections.unique_caveat: The largest exact chains are small, and the hardware concurrence deviates systematically from the ideal prediction; the authors model that suppression with a fitted depolarizing-noise parameter.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three physics categories and combines an exact/theoretical treatment with processor measurements; the authors report a distinctive link between the entropy Jensen gap and Holevo information.

sections.title: First search for sidereal and annual modulation of $Z$-pole asymmetries with the recovered SLD data set
sections.abstract: A time-resolved reanalysis of recovered SLD Z-pole collision data finds no sidereal, solar-diurnal or annual modulation and derives limits on selected anisotropy and Lorentz-violation parameters.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports a statistical 95% C.L. bound of 0.0086 on the sidereal first-harmonic asymmetry amplitude in the main sample and a null check on 229,833 later-run events; the SME mapping is leading order and the stated coefficient constraints exclude finite bands for the families assessed.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; archival reanalysis of polarized SLD/SLC data from 1996–1998, including 385,583 selected hadronic Z decays
sections.unique_caveat: The amplitude limit is statistical, while the mapping to SME coefficients is model-dependent and leading order; the author cautions that some results exclude finite coefficient bands rather than furnishing a simple upper limit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between experiment and phenomenology, it applies a new time-resolved analysis to a public recovered dataset and checks the null result on a later-released run; the paper also proposes a distinct Z-pole birefringence channel.

sections.title: Six New Eclipsing AM CVn Binaries from the Zwicky Transient Facility
sections.abstract: A GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry identifies six eclipsing AM CVn binaries, with Keck spectra confirming helium-dominated, hydrogen-undetected systems at orbital periods of 39.3–59.9 minutes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors classify all six as AM CVn systems from helium emission without detectable hydrogen and identify eclipses with periods between 39.3 and 59.9 minutes.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Zwicky Transient Facility photometry and Keck I/LRIS spectroscopy
sections.unique_caveat: High-speed follow-up is still needed to determine mass ratios, inclinations and component radii; the systems do not yet by themselves settle formation or long-term evolution models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Six new candidates receive spectroscopic classification with Keck/LRIS, and the paper reports increasing the known deeply eclipsing sample from 11 to 17; this is a concrete, multi-object observational release.

sections.title: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
sections.abstract: Variational wavefunctions with neural-network correlations predict competing liquid and crystalline phases for ideal anyons, including candidate phases that the authors connect to reentrant Hall and superconducting behavior in twisted MoTe2.
sections.claimed_result: Within the proposed variational ansatz, the author finds a paired semion superfluid and, for SU(3)-flavor anyons at statistical angle π/3, a chiral color superconductor with lower variational energy than the compared candidate phases.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; variational many-body wavefunctions with numerical energy comparisons, including neural-network correlations
sections.unique_caveat: The phase identification and twisted-MoTe2 connection follow from the variational ansatz and are not an experimental identification; alternative states outside the tested ansätze may change the ordering.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in strongly correlated electrons and mesoscopic/nanoscale physics; the paper compares several explicitly constructed ansätze and connects them to recent fractional-Chern-insulator phenomenology. The material-specific interpretation remains theoretical.
